```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Top-level tmux popup menu — invoked by `prefix + Space`.
3	#
4	# Why a script (not inline `display-menu` in keybindings.conf):
5	#   1. tmux's command parser stops at literal `;`, `{`, `}` even inside
6	#      nested quotes. With ~50 menu rows full of fzf binds and shell
7	#      one-liners, escaping became fragile and broke silently.
8	#   2. tmux `display-menu` does not paginate. If the menu is taller than
9	#      the terminal, the entire popup is suppressed with no error. By
10	#      generating the menu here we can read $TMUX client_height and
11	#      auto-trim low-frequency rows when small.
12	#   3. Submenus are normal `tmux display-menu` invocations from rows;
13	#      they don't share quoting context with the parent menu.
14	#
15	# Submenus live in sibling scripts:
16	#   menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh, menu-sesh.sh,
17	#   menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh, menu-agents.sh
18	#
19	# See: pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md
20	
21	set -euo pipefail
22	
23	H=$(tmux display-message -p '#{client_height}')
24	DIR=~/.config/tmux
25	
26	# Tier 0: ALWAYS shown (highest frequency, ~7 rows + 2 separators)
27	declare -a tier0=(
28	  "Last window"  Tab "last-window"
29	  "Last pane"    P   "last-pane"
30	  ""             ""  ""
31	  "Choose win"   w   "choose-tree -Zw"
32	  "Choose sess"  s   "choose-tree -Zs"
33	  "Pane #s"      q   "display-panes -d 0"
34	  ""             ""  ""
35	  "Sesh picker"  g   "run-shell '$DIR/sesh-picker.sh'"
36	  "Lazygit"      G   "display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' 'lazygit'"
37	)
38	
39	# Tier 1: shown when height >= 22 (adds new-window/split/zoom)
40	declare -a tier1=(
41	  ""             ""  ""
42	  "New window"   c   "new-window -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
43	  "Split |"      "|" "split-window -h -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
44	  "Split -"      "-" "split-window -v -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
45	  "Zoom"         z   "resize-pane -Z"
46	)
47	
48	# Tier 2: submenus + cheatsheet (always shown if Tier 1 is shown)
49	declare -a tier2=(
50	  ""             ""  ""
51	  "→ Layouts"    L   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-layouts.sh'"
52	  "→ Session"    S   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-session.sh'"
53	  "→ Sesh+"      E   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-sesh.sh'"
54	  "→ Agents"     A   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-agents.sh'"
55	  "→ Popups"     o   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-popups.sh'"
56	  "→ Theme"      T   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-theme.sh'"
57	  "→ System"     Y   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-system.sh'"
58	  ""             ""  ""
59	  "Cheatsheet"   "?" "display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' 'glow -p $DIR/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null || less $DIR/cheatsheet.md'"
60	  "Search keys"  "/" "run-shell -b ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/scripts/keybinding.sh"
61	)
62	
63	rows=("${tier0[@]}")
64	if [ "$H" -ge 22 ]; then
65	  rows+=("${tier1[@]}" "${tier2[@]}")
66	elif [ "$H" -ge 14 ]; then
67	  rows+=("${tier2[@]}")
68	fi
69	
70	exec tmux display-menu -T "#[align=centre,bold]tmux (h=$H)" -x R -y P "${rows[@]}"
71
```

```text
28	  "Resize even" "=" "select-layout even-horizontal"
29	  "Mark pane"   m "select-pane -m"
30	  "Swap marked" s "swap-pane"
31	  "Join marked pane here (h-split)" j "join-pane -h ; display-message 'Joined marked pane here'"
32	  "Join marked pane here (v-split)" J "join-pane -v ; display-message 'Joined marked pane here'"
33	  "Send pane to window... (h-split)" S "choose-tree -Zw -F '#{window_name}' \"join-pane -h -s '#{pane_id}' -t '%%' ; display-message 'Sent pane to target'\""
```

```text
2	# Source: dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh (managed by chezmoi)
3	#
4	# Generic per-window tmux status badge helpers — POSIX, sourced by both
5	# zsh and bash. Thin convenience layer over the same primitive workmux
6	# uses (`tmux set-option -w '@<name>_status' '<glyph>'`), so any script /
7	# hook / cron job / build watcher can tag its tmux window without
8	# pulling in workmux.
9	#
10	# Why a shared layer (not in 38_workmux.zsh): these helpers don't need
11	# any zsh feature, and the most common consumers (build scripts, deploy
12	# hooks, CI wrappers) tend to be `#!/bin/bash` or `#!/bin/sh`. Putting
13	# them in dot_config/shell/ means they Just Work from any shell.
14	#
15	# Companion: docs/tools/workmux.md → "Reusing the per-window status
16	# mechanism (without workmux)" for design rationale, the lifecycle hard
17	# rules, and the build-watcher worked example.
18	#
19	# Quick reference:
20	#
21	#   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨           # tag current window
22	#   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨 mysess:3  # tag specific window
23	#   tmux_status_get my_build              # read current window
24	#   tmux_status_clear my_build            # unset (current window)
25	#   tmux_status_clear my_build mysess:3   # unset specific window
26	#   tmux_status_clear_all my_build        # unset across every session
27	#   tmux_status_list                      # list every @*_status user-var
28	#   tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
29	#                                         # set 🔨, run cmd, set ✅/❌
30	#                                         # by exit code, auto-clear on
31	#                                         # signal trap
32	#
33	# Naming convention: pass the LOGICAL name without `@` or `_status`
34	# suffix — these helpers add the `@<name>_status` wrapper. So
35	# `tmux_status_set my_build 🔨` writes `@my_build_status`. This keeps
36	# the user-var namespace tidy (`@<tool>_status` everywhere) and lets
37	# you grep for "every status producer" with `tmux_status_list`.

43	# Internal: validate name (alphanumeric + underscore + dash, no `@` /
44	# `_status` since we add them). Returns 0 if valid, 1 if not (with
45	# stderr diagnostic). Empty name is rejected. Names starting with
46	# `workmux` are reserved to avoid clobbering workmux's own user-var.
47	_tmux_status_validate_name() {
48	    if [ -z "${1:-}" ]; then
49	        printf 'tmux_status: name argument is required\n' >&2
50	        return 1
51	    fi
52	    case "$1" in
53	        workmux*)
54	            # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks here are literal Markdown-style code spans, not command substitution.
55	            printf 'tmux_status: name "%s" reserved (workmux owns @workmux_status). Use `workmux set-window-status` for the agent path.\n' "$1" >&2
56	            return 1
57	            ;;
58	        *[!A-Za-z0-9_-]*)

63	    return 0
64	}

66	# tmux_status_set <name> <glyph> [target]
67	#   target defaults to current window (`tmux display -p '#{session_name}:#{window_index}'`)
68	tmux_status_set() {
69	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
70	    if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then
71	        printf 'tmux_status_set: usage: tmux_status_set <name> <glyph> [target]\n' >&2
72	        return 1
73	    fi

75	    _glyph="$2"

78	        tmux set-option -w -t "$_target" "@${_name}_status" "$_glyph" 2>/dev/null
79	    else

92	    else
93	        tmux show-options -wv "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
94	    fi
95	}

97	# tmux_status_clear <name> [target]
98	tmux_status_clear() {
99	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
100	    _name="$1"

102	    if [ -n "$_target" ]; then
103	        tmux set-option -w -t "$_target" -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
104	    else
105	        tmux set-option -w -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
106	    fi
107	}

109	# tmux_status_clear_all <name>
110	#   walk every window in every session, unset @<name>_status
111	tmux_status_clear_all() {
112	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
113	    _name="$1"

115	        tmux set-option -w -t "$_w" -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
116	    done

119	# tmux_status_list
120	#   show every @*_status user-var across every window (read-only audit)
121	tmux_status_list() {
122	    tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index} #{window_name}' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r _line; do
123	        _w="${_line%% *}"

125	        tmux show-options -w -t "$_w" 2>/dev/null \
126	            | awk -v w="$_line" '/^@[A-Za-z0-9_-]+_status / {print w "  " $0}'

130	# tmux_status_run <name> <working_glyph> <ok_glyph> <fail_glyph> -- <cmd> [args...]
131	#   Run a command, badge the window with `working_glyph` while it runs,
132	#   then `ok_glyph` on success or `fail_glyph` on failure. Traps INT /
133	#   TERM / HUP to clear the badge instead of leaking on Ctrl+C.
134	#
135	#   Example:
136	#     tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
137	#     tmux_status_run deploy   🚀 🟢 🔴 -- ./deploy.sh prod
138	tmux_status_run() {
139	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
140	    if [ $# -lt 6 ]; then
141	        printf 'tmux_status_run: usage: tmux_status_run <name> <working> <ok> <fail> -- <cmd> [args...]\n' >&2
142	        return 1
143	    fi
144	    _name="$1"
145	    _working="$2"
146	    _ok="$3"
147	    _fail="$4"
148	    shift 4
149	    if [ "${1:-}" != "--" ]; then
150	        # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks are literal in the diagnostic message.
151	        printf 'tmux_status_run: missing `--` separator before command\n' >&2
152	        return 1
153	    fi
154	    shift
155	    if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
156	        # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks are literal in the diagnostic message.
157	        printf 'tmux_status_run: no command after `--`\n' >&2
158	        return 1
159	    fi
160	
161	    # Capture target ONCE up front — if `cmd` happens to switch tmux
162	    # window, we still want the badge to land on the window the user
163	    # invoked from.
164	    _target=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}:#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null)
165	    [ -z "$_target" ] && _target=""

167	    # Trap so Ctrl+C / kill doesn't leak the working glyph forever.
168	    # Use a trap that clears, then re-raises the signal default for
169	    # correct exit semantics.
170	    trap '_tmux_status_run_trap "$_name" "$_target"' INT TERM HUP
171	
172	    tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_working" "$_target"
173	    "$@"
174	    _rc=$?
175	    if [ $_rc -eq 0 ]; then
176	        tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_ok" "$_target"
177	    else
178	        tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_fail" "$_target"
179	    fi
180	
181	    trap - INT TERM HUP
182	    return $_rc
183	}
184	
185	# Internal: trap helper for tmux_status_run. Clears the badge then
186	# re-raises the signal so the calling shell sees correct $? / exit code.
187	_tmux_status_run_trap() {
188	    tmux_status_clear "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null
189	    trap - INT TERM HUP
190	    # Re-raise INT (most common case); for TERM/HUP we just let the
191	    # shell continue — calling scripts can decide what to do via $?.
192	    kill -INT $$ 2>/dev/null
193	}
```

```text
3	#
4	# `tsum` — AI-powered overview of every tmux session. Thin POSIX wrapper
5	# around ~/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py (the core script does the
6	# capture, LLM call, 10-min caching, and rendering).
7	#
8	# Why a wrapper at all (not just an alias):
9	#   - `-i` / `--interactive` adds an fzf picker on top of the script's
10	#     `picker` mode and calls `tmux switch-client -t <sess>` on Enter.
11	#     fzf piping is awkward to express as an alias.
12	#   - The wrapper does an early-return-silent dance when tmux isn't on PATH
13	#     (cron, fresh boxes pre-ansible) so calling code can be unconditional.
14	#
15	# See:
16	#   - dot_config/tmux/executable_tmux-session-summary.py (the core)
17	#   - docs/shells/aliases.md (`tsum` row)
18	#   - dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh (shares AICAP_* env vars)
19	#   - dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh (this file's slot-61 neighbour)
20	
21	# Skip silently if tmux isn't installed — POSIX-shared file, may be sourced
22	# inside cron / Docker / headless SSH long before ansible bootstrapped tmux.
23	command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
24	
25	tsum() {
26	    _tsum_script="$HOME/.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py"
27	    if [ ! -x "$_tsum_script" ]; then
28	        printf 'tsum: %s missing or not executable. Run `chezmoi apply` first.\n' "$_tsum_script" >&2
29	        return 1
30	    fi
31	
32	    _tsum_interactive=0
33	    _tsum_forward=""
34	
35	    # POSIX-portable arg parse — `getopts` can't do long flags, so do it by
36	    # hand. Everything except `-i`/`--interactive` is forwarded as-is to the
37	    # Python script (which has its own argparse).
38	    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
39	        case "$1" in
40	            -i|--interactive)
41	                _tsum_interactive=1
42	                ;;
43	            -h|--help)
44	                cat >&2 <<'EOF'
45	tsum — AI-summarize every tmux session
46	
47	USAGE
48	    tsum [list]                 print one-block-per-session summary (default)
49	    tsum picker                 print TSV (session<TAB>line) for fzf piping
50	    tsum -i | --interactive     fzf picker; Enter switches client to that session
51	    tsum -d | --deep            include visible area (20-100 lines) of each
52	                                session's active pane in the LLM prompt
53	    tsum --shallow              force metadata-only (overrides TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT=1)
54	    tsum --sort closability     order keep → check → safe (default: alphabetical)
55	    tsum --only safe|check|keep filter to one closability tier
56	    tsum -r | --refresh         bypass the prompt-hash cache and force a fresh LLM call
57	    tsum --dry-run              print what would be sent to the LLM (no API call)
58	    tsum --no-cache             don't read or write the cache
59	
60	EXAMPLES
61	    tsum --sort closability     active work surfaces first, idle stuff last
62	    tsum --only safe            "what can I close right now?"
63	    tsum picker --only safe -i  fzf-pick a safe-to-close session to switch to
64	
65	ENV
66	    AICAP_AGENT, AICAP_*_MODEL  pin / override the agent (shared with aifix/aiblock)
67	    TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT=1         make --deep implicit (override per-call with --shallow)
68	    TSUM_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL   seconds, default 120. Even when the prompt
69	                                hash differs from the cached one, reuse the
70	                                old summary if the previous LLM call was
71	                                within this window (protects against high-
72	                                volatility deep-mode panes like htop/watch).
73	                                Identical prompts always hit, regardless of
74	                                age. Set to 0 to disable throttling.
75	                                TSUM_CACHE_TTL accepted as fallback alias.
76	    TSUM_TIMEOUT                seconds, default 60
77	    TSUM_TMUX_BIN               full path to tmux binary, default "tmux" (use this
78	                                when multiple tmux binaries are on PATH and the
79	                                server you care about runs from a specific one,
80	                                e.g. TSUM_TMUX_BIN=/bin/tmux)
81	
82	CACHE
83	    $XDG_CACHE_HOME/tmux-session-summary/<hostname>-<mode>.json
84	    (cache key is sha256(build_prompt)[:16] — identical prompts hit forever;
85	     differing prompts trigger a fresh LLM call unless throttled by
86	     TSUM_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL)
87	EOF
88	                return 0
89	                ;;
90	            *)
91	                # Quote each forwarded arg with single quotes; embedded single
92	                # quotes get the '\'' dance so eval-time re-parsing is exact.
93	                _tsum_forward="$_tsum_forward '$(printf %s "$1" | sed "s/'/'\\\\''/g")'"
94	                ;;
95	        esac
96	        shift
97	    done
98	
99	    if [ "$_tsum_interactive" -eq 0 ]; then
100	        # Plain mode — let the script render to stdout/stderr directly.
101	        eval "\"\$_tsum_script\" $_tsum_forward"
102	        return $?
103	    fi
104	
105	    # Interactive: picker | fzf, switch on Enter.
106	    if ! command -v fzf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
```

```text
170	# Capture Pane Helpers
171	# =============================================================================
172	
173	# prefix + y: copy visible pane content to system clipboard
174	# `load-buffer -w -` loads into tmux's paste buffer AND forwards to the outer
175	# terminal via OSC 52 (requires `set-clipboard on` in common.conf). This works
176	# over SSH without shelling out to pbcopy/xclip on the remote host.
177	bind y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -p | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Pane content copied to clipboard'"
178	
179	# prefix + Y: copy full scrollback to system clipboard
180	bind Y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Full scrollback copied to clipboard'"
181	
182	# prefix + C-y: capture pane into fzf for line-by-line selection, yank chosen lines
183	bind C-y run-shell "\
184	  tmux capture-pane -pS - | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% --multi --tac --no-sort \
185	    --header 'Select lines to copy (Tab=multi, Enter=copy)' \
186	    | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Selected lines copied'"
187	
188	# prefix + M-y: copy the LAST command's OUTPUT to clipboard (Warp-style).
189	# Requires OSC 133 markers — if the shell doesn't emit them (non-zsh shell,
190	# DISABLE_OSC133=1, or a remote bash without our hook), selection ends up
191	# empty. Chain: enter copy-mode, jump to start of previous command's output,
192	# begin selection, jump forward to the next prompt (end of output), copy,
193	# flash confirmation.
194	bind M-y copy-mode \; \
195	  send-keys -X previous-prompt -o \; \
196	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
197	  send-keys -X next-prompt \; \
198	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \
199	  display-message "Last command output copied to clipboard"
200	
201	# prefix + M-i: copy the LAST command's INPUT LINE (prompt + typed command).
202	# Same dependency on OSC 133 markers. Because we don't emit the B marker
203	# (end-of-prompt), the copied text includes prompt chrome (e.g. "❯ echo hi"
204	# not just "echo hi"). Trim in the paste target if needed. Chain: enter
205	# copy-mode, jump to the previous prompt's A marker, begin selection, jump
206	# forward to the C marker (= start of output = end of input line), copy.
207	bind M-i copy-mode \; \
208	  send-keys -X previous-prompt \; \
209	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
210	  send-keys -X next-prompt -o \; \
211	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \
212	  display-message "Last command input (prompt+line) copied to clipboard"
213	
214	# =============================================================================
215	# Vim-Style Pane Navigation
216	# =============================================================================
217	
218	bind h select-pane -L
219	bind j select-pane -D
220	bind k select-pane -U
221	bind l select-pane -R
222	
223	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
224	# vim-tmux-navigator: prefix-less Ctrl+h/j/k/l crosses tmux panes <-> vim splits
225	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
226	# Detect if the current pane is running vim/neovim; if so forward the key,
227	# otherwise move between tmux panes. Matches christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator.
228	# Gated on chezmoi `enableVimMode` (default true). When off, Ctrl+h/j/k/l
229	# pass through to the inner shell (Ctrl+L = clear, Ctrl+H = backspace, etc.).
```

```text
483	# =============================================================================
484	# Popup Menu (prefix + Space)
485	# =============================================================================
486	# Two entry keys, same menu. The menu itself is generated by a script
487	# (`~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`) which:
488	#
489	#   1. Reads `#{client_height}` and emits a tier-trimmed row list. tmux's
490	#      `display-menu` does NOT paginate — if the menu is taller than the
491	#      terminal, the entire popup is silently suppressed (no error). The
492	#      script keeps the menu fitting on tiny mobile-SSH heights too.
493	#   2. Submenus are sibling scripts (menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh,
494	#      menu-sesh.sh, menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh). Each
495	#      `exec tmux display-menu …` so quoting context resets per submenu —
496	#      no nested-quote escaping disasters in keybindings.conf.
497	#
498	# History: an earlier flat ~50-row menu silently failed on smaller heights
499	# and was misdiagnosed as a csi-u key encoding bug, then as a quoting bug.
500	# Both real (the `\;` accelerator was broken, sesh fzf binds had nested-
501	# quote issues), but the dominant symptom — "menu doesn't open at all" —
502	# was actually menu-too-tall. See pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md.
503	#
504	# Discovery fallbacks if you forget the keys: `prefix + ?` (tmux-fzf fuzzy
505	# picker over every binding), `prefix + M-/` (glow cheatsheet popup), or
506	# right-click on a pane / status line.
507	
508	unbind-key Space
509	unbind-key Enter
510	bind-key Space run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu.sh"
511	# Note: `prefix + e` was previously a popup-menu alias (added as workaround
512	# for a misdiagnosed display-menu bug — see pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md).
513	# Removed so `e` is free as a sub-menu mnemonic (e.g. "Even layout: horizontal"
514	# in the window right-click menu).
515	
516	# =============================================================================
517	# Right-click menus on the keyboard (prefix + M-p / M-w / M-s)
518	# =============================================================================
519	# Keyboard equivalents of the three MouseDown3* right-click menus defined at
520	# the top of this file:
521	#
522	#   prefix + M-p  →  menu-pane.sh         (same as right-click on a pane)
523	#   prefix + M-w  →  menu-window.sh       (same as right-click on a window tab)
524	#   prefix + M-s  →  menu-status-left.sh  (same as right-click on the session
525	#                                          name in the status-left area)
526	#
527	# WHY scripts (not inline `display-menu` like the MouseDown3* bindings):
528	# `pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md` — a `display-menu` launched
529	# indirectly via `run-shell` from a MouseDown3 binding has its mouse-release
530	# event leaked into the menu, dismissing it instantly. So the MouseDown3*
531	# bodies MUST stay inline above. Keyboard activation has no pending mouse
532	# event, so a script wrapper is safe — and keeps this file shorter. The menu
533	# bodies are duplicated between the MouseDown3* bindings here and the scripts
534	# under dot_config/tmux/menu-*.sh; each location carries a "sync me" comment.
535	#
536	# Requires terminal Option-as-Meta on macOS (already set by the repo's
537	# Ghostty/cmux config: `macos-option-as-alt = left`). On Linux terminals the
538	# Alt modifier is sent natively.
539	
540	bind -N "right-click pane menu (keyboard)"      M-p run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu-pane.sh"
541	bind -N "right-click window menu (keyboard)"    M-w run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu-window.sh"
542	bind -N "right-click status-left menu (keyboard)" M-s run-shell "~/.config/tmux/menu-status-left.sh"
```

```text
57	# OSC 52 clipboard copy: ships stdin bytes through a terminal escape sequence.
58	# Works over SSH with no X/Wayland as long as the terminal (or tmux with
59	# set-clipboard on) forwards OSC 52. Writes to /dev/tty so it is not captured
60	# by an outer pipeline.
61	osc52_copy() {
62	    [[ -w /dev/tty ]] || return 1
63	    command -v base64 >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
64	
65	    local data
66	    data="$(base64 | tr -d '\n')"
67	    [[ -n "$data" ]] || return 0
68	
69	    if [[ -n "${TMUX:-}" ]]; then
70	        # shellcheck disable=SC1003 # printf consumes the backslash escapes.
71	        printf '\033Ptmux;\033\033]52;c;%s\033\033\\\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
72	    else
73	        # shellcheck disable=SC1003 # printf consumes the backslash escapes.
74	        printf '\033]52;c;%s\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
75	    fi
76	}
77

96	
97	    case "$base" in
98	        id_rsa|id_ed25519|id_ecdsa|id_dsa|id_xmss)

100	            ;;
101	    esac
102
```

```text
115:### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
117:`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templated files + 2 first-seed files (`marimo.toml`, btop's `btop.conf`): [docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
122:- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`, `dot_config/opencode/modify_*.json.tmpl`, `dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
185:The popup menu (bound to `prefix + Space` and `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two unrelated tmux quirks force this:
187:1. **Position clamping (tmux ≥ 3.3)**: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) when it would place the menu past the terminal edge. tmux 3.3+ clamps. `devtools` role auto-upgrades on Debian/Ubuntu (Linuxbrew first, else [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage) extracted to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/` with a `~/.local/bin/tmux` shim). Run `tmux kill-server` once after — running servers keep the old binary in memory.
188:2. **Menu-too-tall silent failure (all versions)**: `display-menu` does **not** paginate. Taller than terminal → entire popup suppressed, no error, nothing in `tmux show-messages`. `man tmux`: _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ Misdiagnosed for hours as a CSI-u keysym bug after a 50-row flat menu started failing on smaller heights.
193:- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
194:- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
197:See `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` (red herrings included) and `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
199:### Key tmux settings for coding agents
203:- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps (Claude Code, Neovim, …). **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
205:- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
209:Full tmux config breakdown / theme switching / keybindings / troubleshooting: [docs/tools/tmux/](docs/tools/tmux/).
```

```text
1	# tmux + OSC 133 capture helpers — shell-level counterparts of the
2	# prefix + M-y / M-i tmux bindings, with an N-back index.
3	#
4	#   cpcmd [N]    last (or Nth-latest) command's INPUT  (zsh history; universal)
5	#   cpout [N]    last (or Nth-latest) command's OUTPUT (tmux copy-mode chain)
6	#   cpblock [N]  last (or Nth-latest) command's FULL BLOCK, Warp-style
7	#
8	# N defaults to 1 (= latest). N=2 is the one before that, and so on.
9	#
10	# Each prints captured text to stdout (pipe-friendly: `cpout | grep ERROR`)
11	# AND copies to system clipboard. Diagnostic + byte count go to stderr so
12	# stdout stays clean for pipes.
13	#
14	# WHY cpout/cpblock need tmux:
15	# tmux consumes OSC 133 marker bytes and only stores them as per-line
16	# attributes in its grid — `tmux capture-pane -pe` does NOT re-emit them.
17	# Outside tmux there's no portable way to recover boundaries of a past
18	# command's output (terminals like iTerm2/Ghostty have proprietary APIs,
19	# but nothing cross-terminal). cpcmd uses zsh shell history instead, so it
20	# works universally.
21	#
22	# Requires: zsh; plus tmux for cpout/cpblock.
23	
24	# Pipe stdin to system clipboard, preferring tmux's OSC 52 bridge (SSH-safe)
25	# and falling back to platform-native clipboard tools.
26	_cpx_to_clipboard() {
27	  if [[ -n "$TMUX" ]]; then
28	    tmux load-buffer -w -
29	  elif command -v pbcopy &>/dev/null; then
30	    pbcopy
31	  elif command -v wl-copy &>/dev/null; then
32	    wl-copy
33	  elif command -v xclip &>/dev/null; then
34	    xclip -selection clipboard -in
35	  elif command -v xsel &>/dev/null; then
36	    xsel --clipboard --input
37	  else
38	    cat >/dev/null
39	    return 1
40	  fi
```

## 2. Clipboard/copy helper conventions

Two established patterns, both cross-platform with tmux-OSC52-first ordering:

**(a) The `x` CLI — `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`** (`x copy`, `x copy-file`). The `copy_backend()` (lines 141-189) tries, in order: WSL `clip.exe` → macOS `pbcopy` → Wayland `wl-copy` → X11 `xclip` → `xsel` → OSC 52 fallback. The OSC 52 helper (lines 61-76) is tmux-aware:
```sh
osc52_copy() {
    [[ -w /dev/tty ]] || return 1
    command -v base64 >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    local data
    data="$(base64 | tr -d '\n')"
    [[ -n "$data" ]] || return 0
    if [[ -n "${TMUX:-}" ]]; then
        printf '\033Ptmux;\033\033]52;c;%s\033\033\\\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
    else
        printf '\033]52;c;%s\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
    fi
}
```
So a feature could simply pipe to `x copy` for cross-platform copy. Note: `x copy` is a bash script (uses `[[ ]]`, `local`), invoked as an external command, not sourced.

**(b) The in-shell helper — `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh`** lines 26-41 — the most directly reusable pattern for a shell function that copies, and it prefers tmux's own buffer bridge (which honors `set-clipboard on` → OSC 52):
```sh
_cpx_to_clipboard() {
  if [[ -n "$TMUX" ]]; then
    tmux load-buffer -w -
  elif command -v pbcopy &>/dev/null; then
    pbcopy
  elif command -v wl-copy &>/dev/null; then
    wl-copy
  elif command -v xclip &>/dev/null; then
    xclip -selection clipboard -in
  elif command -v xsel &>/dev/null; then
    xsel --clipboard --input
  else
    cat >/dev/null
    return 1
  fi
}
```
(This uses `[[ ]]` / `&>` — bash/zsh, not strict POSIX. For a shared `dot_config/shell/` file you'd write the POSIX equivalent, or shell out to `x copy`.)

```text
2	# Source: dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh (managed by chezmoi)
3	#
4	# Generic per-window tmux status badge helpers — POSIX, sourced by both
5	# zsh and bash. Thin convenience layer over the same primitive workmux
6	# uses (`tmux set-option -w '@<name>_status' '<glyph>'`), so any script /
7	# hook / cron job / build watcher can tag its tmux window without
8	# pulling in workmux.
9	#
10	# Why a shared layer (not in 38_workmux.zsh): these helpers don't need
11	# any zsh feature, and the most common consumers (build scripts, deploy
12	# hooks, CI wrappers) tend to be `#!/bin/bash` or `#!/bin/sh`. Putting
13	# them in dot_config/shell/ means they Just Work from any shell.
14	#
15	# Companion: docs/tools/workmux.md → "Reusing the per-window status
16	# mechanism (without workmux)" for design rationale, the lifecycle hard
17	# rules, and the build-watcher worked example.
18	#
19	# Quick reference:
20	#
21	#   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨           # tag current window
22	#   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨 mysess:3  # tag specific window
23	#   tmux_status_get my_build              # read current window
24	#   tmux_status_clear my_build            # unset (current window)
25	#   tmux_status_clear my_build mysess:3   # unset specific window
26	#   tmux_status_clear_all my_build        # unset across every session
27	#   tmux_status_list                      # list every @*_status user-var
28	#   tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
29	#                                         # set 🔨, run cmd, set ✅/❌
30	#                                         # by exit code, auto-clear on
31	#                                         # signal trap
32	#
33	# Naming convention: pass the LOGICAL name without `@` or `_status`
34	# suffix — these helpers add the `@<name>_status` wrapper. So
35	# `tmux_status_set my_build 🔨` writes `@my_build_status`. This keeps
36	# the user-var namespace tidy (`@<tool>_status` everywhere) and lets
37	# you grep for "every status producer" with `tmux_status_list`.
38	
39	# Skip silently if tmux isn't on PATH (cron, headless SSH, fresh box
40	# pre-ansible). Producers can call these unconditionally.
41	command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0

45	# stderr diagnostic). Empty name is rejected. Names starting with
46	# `workmux` are reserved to avoid clobbering workmux's own user-var.
47	_tmux_status_validate_name() {
```

# Plan: Copy current tmux pane path (session:window.pane)

## Context

When collaborating with an AI agent inside a shared tmux session, there's currently
no quick way to grab the address of the pane you're looking at. You either want to
reconnect to it later, or tell an agent "operate on *this* pane" — which requires the
tmux target `session:window.pane` (e.g. `main:2.1`).

Today the repo can copy a **session name** (`MouseDown3StatusLeft` menu → "Copy session
name", `keybindings.conf.tmpl:119`) but nothing copies the full pane target. This plan
fills that gap with three coordinated entry points, matching the existing "same verb via
mouse + keyboard + shell" pattern already used across the tmux config:

1. **Right-click menu item** on a pane (`MouseDown3Pane`)
2. **Prefix keybinding** (`prefix + P`)
3. **Shell function** (`tpath`) usable from any shell, pipe-friendly

Decided with the user:
- Clipboard gets the **readable target** `session:window.pane` only.
- The shell function additionally **prints `target` / `pane_id` / `cwd` to stdout** for
  reference (the stable `%N` pane_id and cwd are handy to paste into an agent chat).
- **Yes**, add a prefix keybinding in addition to the menu item + shell alias.

Canonical format string (already used at `dot_config/television/executable_agent-sessions.py:1158`
and `60_tmux_status.sh:164`): `#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}`.

## Changes

### 1. Right-click pane menu item — `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl`

Add one row to the **inline** `MouseDown3Pane` `display-menu` block (currently lines
24–52), in the copy-related area near `"Enter copy mode" "["` (line 50). Use key `y`
(free in this menu; mirrors the `y` used by "Copy session name"):

\```
"Copy pane path" y { set-buffer -w "#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}" ; display-message "Copied pane path: #{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}" } \
\```

Reuse of `set-buffer -w` (tmux buffer + OSC 52 bridge, SSH-safe) matches the existing
"Copy session name" precedent (`keybindings.conf.tmpl:119`) — no capture-pane needed.

**Hard rule (per the inline `*** IF YOU EDIT THE MENU BODY … ***` comment at
`keybindings.conf.tmpl:20` and pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md):** the
mouse menu body MUST stay inline, and the same item MUST be mirrored into the keyboard
script — see step 2. Do NOT extract it into a `run-shell` script for the mouse path
(queued mouse-release dismisses it).

### 2. Keyboard mirror of the pane menu — `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-pane.sh`

Add the matching entry to the `rows=(…)` array (near `"Enter copy mode" "[" …`, line 36),
keeping keys/order identical to the inline mouse menu:

\```
"Copy pane path" y "set-buffer -w '#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}' ; display-message 'Copied pane path: #{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}'"
\```

(This script is the `prefix + M-p` keyboard equivalent.)

### 3. Prefix keybinding — `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl`

Add a direct binding alongside the capture/clipboard helpers (the `prefix + y/Y/C-y`
cluster, ~lines 170–212). Recommend `prefix + P` (capital P):

\```
# Copy current pane path (session:window.pane) to clipboard
bind P run-shell "tmux set-buffer -w \"#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}\" ; tmux display-message \"Copied pane path: #{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}\""
\```

Before finalizing the key: `grep -nE 'bind(-key)?[^-]*[[:space:]]P([[:space:]]|$)'
dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl` to confirm `P` is unused (lowercase `p` =
previous-window default; capital `P` is expected free). Fall back to another free letter
if it clashes.

### 4. Shell function — new file `dot_config/shell/63_tmux_path.sh`

Next free slot in the tmux cluster (`60_tmux_status.sh`, `61_tmux_summary.sh`,
`62_agent_wakeup.sh`). POSIX, sourced by both shells. Follow the `60_tmux_status.sh`
header style (source-path comment + doc pointer + `command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
return 0` guard).

Behavior of `tpath`:
- Guard: if not inside tmux (`[ -z "${TMUX:-}" ]`), print a hint to stderr and return 1.
- Single query, tab-separated:
  `tmux display-message -p '#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}\t#{pane_id}\t#{pane_current_path}'`
- Copy **only the target** to the clipboard via `tmux set-buffer -w -- "$target"`
  (consistent with the menu/keybinding; OSC 52 bridge honors `set-clipboard on`).
- Print to stdout for reference (pipe-friendly):
  \```
  target : main:2.1
  pane_id: %5
  cwd    : /Users/you/project
  \```
- Emit "copied" confirmation to **stderr** (so stdout stays clean for piping, e.g.
  `tpath | head -1`).

Rationale for `set-buffer -w` over the `_cpx_to_clipboard`/`x copy` backends: the
function is guaranteed to run inside tmux (guarded), so tmux's own OSC 52 bridge is the
simplest cross-platform + SSH-safe path and matches the menu item exactly.

### 5. Docs — `docs/shells/aliases.md`

Add a row to the **`## Tmux Integration`** section table (starts line 729), 4-column
format `| Command | Type | Source File | Description |`:

\```
| `tpath` | function | `dot_config/shell/63_tmux_path.sh` | Print (`target`/`pane_id`/`cwd`) + copy the current pane's `session:window.pane` target to the clipboard — for reconnecting or telling an agent which pane to act on. |
\```

### 6. tmux cheatsheet (if the new binding should be discoverable)

Add `prefix + P` and the "Copy pane path" menu item to `dot_config/tmux/cheatsheet.md`
in the copy/clipboard section, matching how `prefix + y/Y` are listed. Optional but
keeps the popup cheatsheet accurate.

## Cross-file rules honored

- **Menu dual-write** (inline `MouseDown3Pane` ↔ `menu-pane.sh`) — mandatory per the
  inline comment + pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md. Both edited in steps
  1 & 2.
- **CLAUDE.md**: "Alias / shell function in `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/`" → row in
  `docs/shells/aliases.md` (step 5).
- **CLAUDE.md**: keybinding change → cross-check namespace and update
  `docs/shells/keybindings.md` if it documents prefix bindings; add to cheatsheet
  (step 6). This is a `prefix + P` binding (not a root `Ctrl-`/`Alt-` binding), so it
  cannot shadow inner apps — low collision risk, but still grep-verify `P` is free.

## Verification (end-to-end)

1. Render + apply: `chezmoi diff dot_config/tmux/ dot_config/shell/63_tmux_path.sh`,
   then `chezmoi apply`.
2. Reload tmux config: `tmux source-file ~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` (should report no
   parse errors — display-menu is unforgiving of quoting; see
   pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md).
3. **Right-click** a pane → choose "Copy pane path" → confirm the status line shows
   `Copied pane path: <sess>:<win>.<pane>` and paste (`prefix + ]` or system paste)
   yields the correct target.
4. **Keyboard menu**: `prefix + M-p` → "Copy pane path" behaves identically.
5. **Prefix binding**: `prefix + P` → same confirmation + clipboard content.
6. **Shell function**: open a new shell, run `tpath` → verify the 3 stdout lines, the
   stderr "copied" note, and that the clipboard holds only `session:window.pane`. Test
   `tpath | head -1` pipes cleanly. Run under bash too (`bash -c 'source
   ~/.config/shell/63_tmux_path.sh; tpath'`) to confirm POSIX-safety.
7. Verify the pane menu still fits (it grows by 1 row) — retest at terminal heights ~14
   / 22 / 60 per the display-menu height-fit rule (menu is inline, not tiered, so this
   is just a sanity check that it isn't silently suppressed on short terminals).

```text
Today the repo can copy a **session name** (`MouseDown3StatusLeft` menu → "Copy session
name", `keybindings.conf.tmpl:119`) but nothing copies the full pane target. This plan
fills that gap with three coordinated entry points, matching the existing "same verb via
mouse + keyboard + shell" pattern already used across the tmux config:

1. **Right-click menu item** on a pane (`MouseDown3Pane`)
2. **Prefix keybinding** (`prefix + P`)
3. **Shell function** (`tpath`) usable from any shell, pipe-friendly

Decided with the user:
- Clipboard gets the **readable target** `session:window.pane` only.
- The shell function additionally **prints `target` / `pane_id` / `cwd` to stdout** for
  reference (the stable `%N` pane_id and cwd are handy to paste into an agent chat).
- **Yes**, add a prefix keybinding in addition to the menu item + shell alias.

Canonical format string (already used at `dot_config/television/executable_agent-sessions.py:1158`
and `60_tmux_status.sh:164`): `#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}`.
```

```

Reuse of `set-buffer -w` (tmux buffer + OSC 52 bridge, SSH-safe) matches the existing
```

```text
205	# copy-mode, jump to the previous prompt's A marker, begin selection, jump
```

```sh
# ~/.config/shell/63_tmux_path.sh
# Source: dot_config/shell/63_tmux_path.sh (managed by chezmoi)
#
# `tpath` — print + copy the CURRENT tmux pane's address, POSIX, sourced by
# both zsh and bash. Copies the readable target `session:window.pane` (e.g.
# `main:2.1`) to the system clipboard via tmux's OSC 52 bridge, and prints
# `target` / `pane_id` / `cwd` to stdout for reference.
#
# Why: when a human and an AI agent share a tmux session, you need a quick way
# to grab the pane you're looking at — to reconnect later, or to tell the agent
# "operate on THIS pane" (`tmux capture-pane -pt <target>` /
# `tmux send-keys -t <target> ...`). The stable `pane_id` (%N, survives
# window/pane reordering) and cwd are printed alongside so you can paste the
# richer form into an agent chat when the readable target isn't enough.
#
# GUI/keyboard equivalents (same "Copy pane path" action):
#   - right-click a pane → "Copy pane path"   (MouseDown3Pane menu)
#   - prefix + M-p → "Copy pane path"          (menu-pane.sh)
#   - prefix + P                               (direct keybinding)
# All defined in dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl + menu-pane.sh.
#
# stdout is kept pipe-clean (`tpath | head -1` yields the target line); the
# "copied" confirmation goes to stderr.

# Skip silently if tmux isn't on PATH (cron, headless SSH, fresh box).
command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0

# tpath — copy current pane's session:window.pane to clipboard, print details.
tpath() {
    if [ -z "${TMUX:-}" ]; then
        printf 'tpath: not inside a tmux session\n' >&2
        return 1
    fi

    _tpath_target=$(tmux display-message -p '#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}')
    _tpath_id=$(tmux display-message -p '#{pane_id}')
    _tpath_cwd=$(tmux display-message -p '#{pane_current_path}')

    # Copy ONLY the readable target. `set-buffer -w` loads tmux's paste buffer
    # AND forwards via OSC 52 (needs `set-clipboard on` in common.conf) — works
    # over SSH without shelling out to pbcopy/xclip on the remote host.
    tmux set-buffer -w "$_tpath_target"

    printf 'target : %s\n' "$_tpath_target"
    printf 'pane_id: %s\n' "$_tpath_id"
    printf 'cwd    : %s\n' "$_tpath_cwd"
    printf 'Copied pane path: %s\n' "$_tpath_target" >&2

    unset _tpath_target _tpath_id _tpath_cwd
}

```

```text
127	## Capture pane → clipboard

145	## Popup Menu Structure (`prefix + Space`)
146	
147	Generated by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`. The top menu auto-trims based on terminal height — `display-menu` does **not** paginate, so an oversized menu would silently fail to open. Three tiers:
148	
149	- **Always shown** (~9 rows): `Last window` (Tab), `Last pane` (P), `Choose win` (w), `Choose sess` (s), `Pane #s` (q), `Sesh picker` (g), `Lazygit` (G).
150	- **Height ≥ 14**: adds the submenu launchers, `Cheatsheet` (?), `Search keys` (/).
151	- **Height ≥ 22**: also adds `New window` (c), `Split |` (|), `Split -` (-), `Zoom` (z).
152	
153	### Submenus
154	
155	| Top-menu row | Key | Items |
156	|--------------|-----|-------|
157	| `→ Layouts` | L | Even h/v (1/2), Main h/v (3/4), Tiled (5), Resize 75% (+), Pane h/j/k/l, Swap `{`/`}` |
158	| `→ Session` | S | Rename session/window (`$`/`,`), New session (N), Move window (m), Break pane (r), Link window (K), Kill pane/session/all (x/X/Q), Forget auto-restore (F) |
159	| `→ Sesh+` | E | TV picker (V), Built-in (O), Windows (W), Last sesh (U), Repo root (9), CLI Tools tv (B) |
160	| `→ Popups` | o | Lazygit (g), Shell (s), Floax scratchpad (f) |
161	| `→ Theme` | T | Catppuccin (c), tmux2k (t) |
162	| `→ System` | Y | Reload config (R), Install/Update plugins (I/U), Detach (d), Clock (k) |
163

166	| Right-click on… | Mouse | Keyboard | Menu items |

169	| Window tab | `MouseDown3Status` | `prefix + M-w` | Layouts / move/link window / break panes / kill window / bookmarks |
170	| Status-left (session name) | `MouseDown3StatusLeft` | `prefix + M-s` | Next/prev/choose session / copy session name / kill session / kill session & exit / kill all sessions / forget auto-restore |
```

Done. Test buffers cleaned up. Here's what I implemented and verified.

## Summary

A "copy current pane path" (`session:window.pane`) feature with three coordinated entry points, for reconnecting or telling an AI agent which pane to act on.

**Files changed:**
| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl` | "Copy pane path" (`y`) added inline to the `MouseDown3Pane` right-click menu; new `bind C-p` in the Capture Pane Helpers cluster |
| `dot_config/tmux/executable_menu-pane.sh` | Mirror "Copy pane path" (`y`) row (keyboard `prefix + M-p`) — mandatory dual-write per the flash-and-gone pitfall |
| `dot_config/shell/63_tmux_path.sh` | **New** — POSIX `tpath` function: copies the readable target, prints `target`/`pane_id`/`cwd` to stdout, confirmation to stderr |
| `docs/shells/aliases.md` | Row in § Tmux Integration |
| `dot_config/tmux/cheatsheet.md` | `prefix + C-p` entry + updated pane right-click menu description |

**Key adjustment during implementation:** the planned `prefix + P` collided with the **tmux-floax** plugin (a plugin-registered binding my initial grep of the config file couldn't see), and lowercase `p` is `previous-window`. Switched to the free **`prefix + C-p`** (mnemonic: copy path, sits beside `C-y` in the copy cluster).

**Verified end-to-end:**
- `chezmoi apply` + `tmux source-file` parse cleanly (display-menu quoting is unforgiving — it passed).
- `bind C-p` registered; floax's `P` intact.
- `tpath` passes `bash -n`/`sh -n`; a live throwaway-session run produced the 3 stdout lines, the stderr note, and a clipboard buffer holding **only** `session:window.pane`.
- `mkdocs build --strict` surfaces only pre-existing zh-TW anchor-drift (tracked in `backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md`) — nothing from my edits.

One side effect of testing: your system clipboard currently holds a test value (`tpath_test:1.1` was the last thing copied via the OSC 52 bridge). Nothing else outstanding — I have not committed anything.

To use it now in your existing panes, reload each attached client's config (already sourced on the server) — or just try `prefix + C-p`, right-click a pane → "Copy pane path", or run `tpath` in a new shell.
